Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: one aligned damage-state game sprite, transparent PNG. Edit target: supplied intact starship image. Make a LIGHT DAMAGE version of THIS EXACT SHIP. Light damage at 65% hull. Already visibly battle-scarred: multiple deep blackened penetrating craters across port upper saucer around (300,240), starboard mid saucer (745,430), engineering hull (515,1020), and starboard nacelle (830,1030). Torn metal lips, peeled plates exposing ribs and cables, scorched streaks. A small jagged notch torn from saucer rim near (200,270). Nacelles and overall outline still present. Roughly 10-15% of plating damaged. Strong readable physical damage, not just discoloration.
Invariants: original full 1024x1536 portrait canvas, straight overhead view, bow at top, absolutely same ship scale, pixel registration, center position and perspective. Original saucer center approximately (512,410), orange nacelle caps (193,724) and (831,724), engineering fuselage from (512,800) to (512,1340), nacelles down to y1480. Surviving parts MUST stay at the original coordinates; missing parts become transparency, never shrink/recenter/rearrange the wreck. Preserve original silver-gray materials and surface details on surviving hull. Preserve the identity I.S.S. ENTERPRISE NCC-1701 where the remaining plating survives; it is okay for damage to physically destroy portions of those markings.
Damage must be physical modeled torn geometry, with irregular sharp ruptures, layered deck edges and blackened metallic structure. Keep it recognizably the same design. Change only damage, not ship design. Actual alpha transparency outside physical hull AND through removed hull sections. No black/gray backdrop, no haze, no smoke clouds, no drop shadow, no loose flying debris outside hull, no labels or stage text, no collage, no multiple ships. Exposed interiors may have tiny ember glow but do not paint large flames; game adds animated fire later. Return one complete aligned sprite at original canvas dimensions.
